items.item: asynchronous commit is an option that allows transactions to complete more quickly, at the cost that the most recent transactions may be lost if the database should crash

items.item: The commit-latency claim deliberately gives every transaction identical, zero-cost execution time, so any spread in commit latency measured afterward is attributable entirely to the shared flush's own timing, not to any difference in the transactions' own work.

items.item: A false promise is defined precisely as the acknowledgment tick being at or before the crash tick while the durable tick is strictly after it, rather than simply checking whether the crash happened before durability, so that a transaction never acknowledged early in the first place is correctly never flagged regardless of when the crash lands.

items.item: The whole simulation runs on a discrete logical tick counter rather than real wall-clock timing or real threads, so every one of this topic's own measurements is exactly reproducible; no claim here depends on scheduler timing or measured wall-clock durations.

items.item: The leader in this topic's own group-commit implementation is simply whichever transaction has the earliest ready tick, matching PostgreSQL's own words directly: the first process ready to flush waits out the configured interval while every later-arriving process only waits for that leader's own flush to finish.
